title: Why Is Planet Fitness So Cheap?
description:
Planet Fitness has 21.5 million members but fewer than 3,000 gyms, more than 7,000 members per club, so its cheap memberships only work if most people stay home.
#planetfitness #gym #money #shorts

Sources: Planet Fitness third quarter 2026 results via PR Newswire/Finviz (Nov 5, 2026); Sherwood News (May 2, 2024; Feb 25, 2026); Fortune (Nov 21, 2013); Wikipedia; Planet Fitness (company history and Pizza Monday story); CBS News (May 9, 2024); CNN via ABC7 (May 10, 2024); Business Insider (Dec 2015)
Photos: JeepersMedia (Mike Mozart), DieselDemon, apasciuto, blacklerphotos (CC BY 2.0, Flickr); rawpixel (CC0)

first_comment: Be honest: do you actually go to your gym, or just keep paying for it? 🏋️

scenes.say: Planet Fitness makes money when you don't show up.
scenes.source: Point of view supported by: Sherwood News May 2 2024 ('Planet Fitness' business only works out if its members don't'; model 'predicated on most of its members 1) not working out, while 2) continuing to pay'); The Bear Cave Jan 2023 ('Many never go to the gym'); numbers in scenes 2-3.

scenes.say: {21.5 million|Twenty one and a half million} members. Fewer than {3,000|three thousand} gyms.
scenes.source: Planet Fitness Q3 2026 results, Nov 5 2026 (PR Newswire via Finviz): 'As of September 30, 2026, Planet Fitness had approximately 21.5 million members and 2,962 clubs in all 50 states'; 'system-wide total clubs to 2,962'. Sherwood News Feb 25 2026: 20.8 million members (earlier count).

scenes.say: That's over {7,000|seven thousand} members per gym. No gym floor fits that.
scenes.source: 21.5M / 2,962 = 7,259 (Q3 2026 release). Sherwood News May 2 2024: 'the company averages 7,262 members for each location'; Feb 25 2026: '7,262 members at its peak two years ago'. Club capacities ~200-350 (Sherwood 2024, local reps), but the line only states the obvious (no floor holds 7,000), so no capacity figure is shown.

scenes.say: It only works because most of them stay home.
scenes.source: Sherwood News May 2 2024: business model 'predicated on most of its members 1) not working out, while 2) continuing to pay'; peak attendance '50-60 people working out at a time' per local reps. Fortune 2013: 'the average customer only comes in a couple of days a week.'

scenes.say: In {1992|nineteen ninety two}, two brothers bought a failing gym.
scenes.source: Wikipedia: 'In 1992, Planet Fitness founders Michael and Marc Grondahl acquired a struggling Gold's Gym franchise in Dover, New Hampshire.' Fortune Nov 21 2013: 'Rondeau's partners purchased a failing Gold's Gym in Dover, N.H., renaming it Planet Fitness'. Planet Fitness about page: founded in 1992 in Dover, NH. Photo is a generic old Gold's Gym floor (archival look), not the Dover club.

scenes.say: By {1998|nineteen ninety eight}, it cost {$10|ten dollars} a month, and stayed there {26|twenty six} years.
scenes.source: CBS News May 9 2024: Classic membership 'up from the $10 it had been priced at since 1998', new price $15 for new members from summer 2024. CNN via ABC7 May 10 2024: 'raise the basic plan by 50% for the first time since 1998'; headline 'for 1st time in 26 years'.

scenes.say: But here's the interesting part: they don't want gym rats.
scenes.source: Business Insider Dec 2015, CEO Chris Rondeau: 'We're going after the first time exercises or casual user' and 'Gym intimidation is real.' Wikipedia: model 'focused on the needs of occasional or first-time health club members.' CNN via ABC7 2024 and Entrepreneur 2020: 40% of (new) members never belonged to a gym before.

scenes.say: A lunk alarm goes off if you grunt or drop weights.
scenes.source: Wikipedia: Lunk Alarm, 'a loud siren and rotating light that may be used when a weightlifter grunts too loudly or drops weights.' Business Insider Dec 2015: 'A lunk alarm goes off if people exert themselves with too much machismo.'

scenes.say: And for years, members got free pizza once a month.
scenes.source: Planet Fitness 'real story behind Pizza Monday': free pizza 'on the first Monday night of each month', a tradition 'since 1999'. Business Insider Dec 2015: 'serves free pizza on the first Monday of the month', 'once-a-month pizza nights in all our locations'. Wikipedia: Pizza Monday launched 1999, 'this ended in 2020' (hence 'for years', past tense).

scenes.say: The perfect member pays every month and stays home. Which is exactly why
scenes.source: Point of view from scenes 2-9 (Sherwood News 2024: model relies on members 'continuing to pay' while not working out). Loop line into the hook ('Which is exactly why / Planet Fitness makes money when you don't show up').
